hints: Look closely at the very tips of the Y-shaped molecule. Where would an antigen actually fit and bind on each arm?

Remember an antibody is made of 4 chains: 2 long heavy chains that match each other, and 2 short light chains that match each other. Which labels are the two long stems, and which labels are a heavy tip plus light tip pair?
walkthrough:
**Recall the antibody plan**

Think of an antibody as a Y made of 4 polypeptides. There are 2 long heavy chains forming the stem and inner arms, and 2 short light chains forming the outer arms.

In this diagram, V and U are the two long heavy chains, while P with W is one light chain and S with T is the other light chain.

**Find the antigen-binding sites**

The binding site is at the tip of each arm. It is formed by the variable regions of one heavy chain plus one light chain working together.

On the left that is P and Q together, and on the right that is R and S together. So both P and Q, and R and S, are correct examples of a binding site pair.

**Find the identical pair**

The two heavy chains in one antibody are identical to each other in amino acid sequence. The two light chains are also identical to each other.

That means V (left heavy) and U (right heavy) are identical. The only row that pairs a true binding site (R and S) with a true identical pair (U and V) is row C.

options.A: P and Q do form a binding site, but R and S do not have identical sequences because R is part of a heavy chain and S is part of a light chain.
options.B: Q and V are parts of the same heavy chain, not a binding site pair, and P and S are on different arms so this row mixes up both ideas.
options.C: R and S are the heavy variable plus light variable tips of the right arm so they form one antigen-binding site, and U and V are the two heavy chains which are identical.
options.D: U and V are in the constant stem region and do not bind antigen, even though Q and R (the two heavy variable regions) are in fact identical.
